patterns.name: ToolUse (#02)
patterns.description: The model is handed tools. Each round it either calls one (the harness executes it for real and feeds the result back) or gives the final answer — the simplest decide → act → observe loop.
patterns.recommended_for: Anything needing live data or actions: web lookups, calculators, internal APIs.

patterns.name: ReAct (#03)
patterns.description: Interleaves an explicit written Thought before every Action, then reads the Observation — the visible reasoning trace steers each next tool call.
patterns.recommended_for: Multi-hop research: 'find X, then use X to find Y', debugging with searches.

patterns.name: Planning (#04)
patterns.description: First decomposes the goal into an ordered step list, then executes the steps one by one, replanning when a result changes the picture — plan and execution are separate concerns.
patterns.recommended_for: Long multi-part deliverables: itineraries, migration checklists, briefs.

patterns.name: BrowserAgent (#34b)
patterns.one_liner: REAL Chromium via Playwright + safety gate
patterns.description: The real thing: headless Chromium via Playwright — navigate, read the page, click, extract — with every URL checked against a domain blocklist and outputs scanned for sensitive patterns.
patterns.recommended_for: Web tasks needing a real page: reading a heading, scraping a value, guided navigation.

patterns.name: SWEAgent (#33)
patterns.description: A coding agent with file tools in a sandboxed working dir: it lists and reads files, writes edits, and calls run_check to execute the code — navigate, fix, verify.
patterns.recommended_for: Repo-level bug fixes with a runnable check.

patterns.name: PEV (#06)
patterns.description: Plans steps, executes each one, and a verifier gates EVERY step — a failed step is retried with the verifier's critique attached before the plan may continue.
patterns.recommended_for: Pipelines where one silently-wrong middle step poisons the rest: data transforms, multi-step calculations.

patterns.name: Reflection (#01)
patterns.description: Drafts an answer (generate), has a judge score and critique it 1–10 (critique), then rewrites using that critique (refine) — looping until the score clears the target or iterations run out.
patterns.recommended_for: Quality-over-latency outputs: reports, emails, code snippets, marketing copy.

patterns.name: SelfDiscover (#19)
patterns.description: Composes its own reasoning recipe before solving: SELECTs useful thinking modules, ADAPTs them to this task, assembles an IMPLEMENT plan, then SOLVEs by following it.
patterns.recommended_for: Novel or unusual problems where no standard recipe obviously applies.

patterns.name: ChainOfVerification (#20)
patterns.description: Drafts a baseline answer, plans independent verification questions (plan), answers each one separately so errors can't defend themselves, then rewrites keeping only what survived.
patterns.recommended_for: Hallucination-prone factual output: lists, bios, citations.

patterns.name: ConstitutionalAI (#32)
patterns.description: Checks the draft against an explicit rule list — each rule gets its own pass/fail (critique) — then revises to fix exactly the failed rules. Principles, not vibes.
patterns.recommended_for: Enforcing brand, safety, or style policies on outputs.

patterns.name: Reflexion (#18)
patterns.description: Attempts the task, evaluates its own answer, writes a verbal lesson into episodic memory (reflect), and retries informed by its accumulated lessons — improvement across trials.
patterns.recommended_for: Tasks with a checkable success signal where retries help: code fixes, puzzles.

patterns.name: CorrectiveRAG (#24)
patterns.one_liner: Grade docs, fall back when weak
patterns.description: Retrieves, then GRADES each document's relevance; weak evidence triggers a corrective fallback (query rewrite / web search) before any answer is written.
patterns.recommended_for: RAG over patchy indexes where bad retrievals are common.

patterns.name: AgenticRAG (#23)
patterns.one_liner: Agent decides when & what to retrieve
patterns.description: The agent DECIDES if and what to retrieve — possibly several rounds, reformulating its query each time — instead of blindly stuffing top-k chunks into context.
patterns.recommended_for: Corpus Q&A with multi-hop or ambiguous questions.

patterns.name: SelfRAG (#25)
patterns.description: Emits reflection tokens about each retrieved passage — retrieve? relevant? supported? — and only answers from passages it explicitly endorsed.
patterns.recommended_for: RAG that must be faithful and citable.

patterns.name: AdaptiveRAG (#26)
patterns.description: Classifies query complexity FIRST, then routes: simple → answer directly, moderate → one retrieval, complex → multi-step retrieval — effort proportional to need.
patterns.recommended_for: Mixed traffic where most queries don't need the expensive path.

patterns.name: GraphRAG (#27)
patterns.description: Builds a knowledge graph from the corpus, detects communities of related entities, and pre-summarizes each; global questions are answered from community summaries, not raw chunks.
patterns.recommended_for: 'Themes across the whole corpus' questions that chunk-RAG can't see.

patterns.name: EpisodicSemanticAgent (#08)
patterns.description: Remembers two ways at once: recall past turns + known facts from both memories (retrieve), reply (answer), then WRITE BACK — distill new (subject, predicate, object) triples into the semantic graph (extract) and file the whole turn into episodic memory (record).
patterns.recommended_for: Assistants that must remember users across sessions: preferences, profile facts, decisions.

patterns.name: GraphMemoryAgent (#12)
patterns.description: ingest() distills documents into a knowledge graph of triples; a question extracts its entities, walks the graph around them, and answers strictly from the connected facts it finds.
patterns.recommended_for: Q&A over interlinked entities: org structures, product catalogs, specs.

patterns.name: MemGPT (#31)
patterns.description: Operating-system-style memory: a small always-in-context core plus archival storage, with the agent paging facts in and out itself — virtual memory for conversations.
patterns.recommended_for: Long-running chats that outgrow the context window.

patterns.name: Voyager (#29)
patterns.description: Writes Python skills, EXECUTES them for real in a subprocess, keeps the ones that work in a vector-indexed library, and composes past skills into new ones — a growing toolbox.
patterns.recommended_for: Recurring programmatic tasks that should get faster every time.

patterns.name: AgentWorkflowMemory (#35)
patterns.description: After each solved task it mines a reusable 3–6-step recipe (extract) and indexes it; a new task retrieves the closest recipe (retrieve) and follows it instead of starting cold.
patterns.recommended_for: Task families you solve repeatedly — the second one should be faster than the first.

patterns.name: MentalLoop (#10)
patterns.description: Imagines candidate actions, simulates each one's outcome, scores the simulations with a deterministic rubric, commits to the winner, and explains the trade-off it accepted.
patterns.recommended_for: Decisions with real trade-offs: pick-a-strategy, resource allocation, option calls.

patterns.name: TreeOfThoughts (#09)
patterns.description: Instead of one chain of reasoning: propose K deliberately-different next thoughts (generate), judge each on a strict 1–5 rubric (score), keep only the top beam (prune), and loop deeper — the best complete path wins.
patterns.recommended_for: Problems where the first idea is often wrong: math, constraint puzzles, tricky planning.

patterns.name: SelfConsistency (#21)
patterns.description: Samples N diverse reasoning paths for the same question and majority-votes the final answers — correct reasoning converges while mistakes scatter.
patterns.recommended_for: Math and logic one-shots where a single chain is flaky.

patterns.name: LATS (#22)
patterns.description: Monte-Carlo tree search over reasoning moves: pick the most promising leaf by UCB1 (select), generate K candidate next moves (expand), judge each with a deterministic reward rubric (evaluate), then propagate the reward up the tree (backup) — and loop.
patterns.recommended_for: Hard search problems worth many calls: agent trajectories, game-like tasks.

patterns.name: Ensemble (#13)
patterns.description: Fires N independent voters at the same task and aggregates their answers (majority vote or weighting) — independent errors cancel, agreement survives.
patterns.recommended_for: Cheap reliability boosts on short factual or numeric answers.

patterns.name: MultiAgent (#05)
patterns.description: A supervisor routes the task to specialist agents (each with its own tools and persona), collects their contributions, and a writer synthesizes one answer.
patterns.recommended_for: Work spanning domains: research + numbers + copy in one deliverable.

patterns.name: Blackboard (#07)
patterns.description: All specialists share one workspace. Each round every agent bids on whether it can contribute (bidding), the best bid writes to the board (act), and the loop repeats until synthesize merges the board into the final answer.
patterns.recommended_for: Open-ended creative or analysis work where you can't script who should speak when.

patterns.name: MetaController (#11)
patterns.description: A router over other architectures: classifies the incoming task and dispatches it to the best-fitting pattern in its roster (here planning vs reflection), returning that pattern's result.
patterns.recommended_for: A front door for mixed workloads — one endpoint, many task shapes.

patterns.name: Debate (#28)
patterns.one_liner: N agents argue for K rounds
patterns.description: N agents answer independently, then read each other's positions and argue across K rounds (the round loop), before a judge/vote settles the disagreement (vote).
patterns.recommended_for: Contested questions where single-model bias is the worry.

patterns.name: STORM (#30)
patterns.description: Spawns multiple personas (perspectives), each interviews the topic with pointed questions, answers ground them, an outline organizes it all, and write produces the article.
patterns.recommended_for: Long-form balanced research: wiki-style articles, briefing docs.

patterns.name: DryRun (#14)
patterns.description: Nothing executes directly: the agent proposes an action, a simulator predicts its effect, and a reviewer approves or blocks BEFORE anything runs — destructive requests die in review.
patterns.recommended_for: Any agent allowed near real systems: shell commands, DB writes, outbound email.

patterns.name: ReflexiveMetacognitive (#17)
patterns.description: Before answering, the agent assesses its OWN competence for this request and routes accordingly: answer, hedge with caveats, or escalate to a human — self-awareness as a safety gate.
patterns.recommended_for: High-stakes triage: medical, legal, financial questions.

patterns.name: ComputerUse (#34)
patterns.description: Drives a (mock) GUI through a strict loop: observe screen state, choose ONE categorical action (navigate / click / type), pass a deterministic safety gate, repeat.
patterns.recommended_for: Studying the computer-use loop and safety gating without a real browser.

patterns.name: RLHFSelfImprovement (#15)
patterns.description: Generates candidates, scores them across explicit dimensions with deterministic rubrics, archives the best-so-far, and iterates against its own archive — self-play for quality.
patterns.recommended_for: Squeezing quality on small artifacts: taglines, prompts, product copy.

patterns.name: CellularAutomata (#16)
patterns.one_liner: LLM rules over a grid world
patterns.description: A grid where every cell is a tiny LLM agent that reads its neighbours and an English rule, then updates in sync each step — global behaviour emerges from purely local decisions.

default_kwargs.rule_prompt: A 'tree' cell next to a 'fire' cell becomes 'fire'. 'fire' becomes 'ash' next step. 'ash' stays 'ash'. 'empty' stays 'empty'.

patterns.recommended_for: Simulations and emergence demos: spread models, ecosystem toys.
